title: Selection Sort
objectives: Understand the logic of selection sort: find the smallest, put it at the front
Tell the difference between bubble sort and selection sort

hook.text: In lesson 5.4 you learned to find the smallest element in an array. What if you did that again and again, and each time put what you found at the front?

concept.heading: Find the smallest, put it at the front
concept.body: Selection sort applies the "find the smallest" algorithm from lesson 5.4 over and over: it finds the smallest element in the unsorted part of the array and swaps it with the FIRST element of the unsorted part. This makes the sorted part one element bigger.

concept.heading: How it differs from bubble sort
concept.body: Bubble sort keeps making swaps between NEIGHBORS (many small swaps). Selection sort makes ONLY ONE swap in each pass (after it has found the smallest). Both make a similar number of comparisons, but selection sort involves fewer swaps.

workedExamples.prompt: Sort the array [5, 2, 4] with selection sort.
workedExamples.runnerSource:
numbers ← [5, 2, 4]
FOR i ← 0 TO 1 STEP 1
  smallestIndex ← i
  FOR j ← i + 1 TO 2 STEP 1
    IF numbers[j] < numbers[smallestIndex]
      smallestIndex ← j
    END
  END_LOOP
  temp ← numbers[i]
  numbers[i] ← numbers[smallestIndex]
  numbers[smallestIndex] ← temp
END_LOOP
WRITE numbers[0]
WRITE numbers[1]
WRITE numbers[2]

steps.explain: i = 0: while looking for the smallest, smallestIndex = 1 (value 2) is found.
i = 1: numbers[2] = 4 is smaller than numbers[1] = 5, so they are swapped → [2, 4, 5].

exercises.question: How many swaps does selection sort make in each pass?

feedback.correct: Correct. Each pass just finds the smallest and makes a SINGLE swap.
feedback.incorrect: Selection sort finds the smallest in each pass and makes only ONE swap.

exercises.question: What is the main difference between selection sort and bubble sort?
options: Selection sort makes no comparisons at all
Bubble sort keeps swapping neighbors, while selection sort makes only one swap per pass
Selection sort only works on text

feedback.correct: Correct. They differ in the number of swaps.
feedback.incorrect: Bubble sort makes many neighbor swaps; selection sort makes only one swap per pass (the one that brings the smallest to the front).

exercises.question: What does this code write to the screen?
exercises.hint: In [3, 1, 2], the smallest, 1, is brought to the front, then 2, and then 3 is left.

exercises.question: Put the steps in one pass of selection sort in the correct order.
steps: Find the smallest element in the unsorted part
Record the index of the smallest
Swap the smallest with the first element of the unsorted part

exercises.question: The "find the smallest" step of selection sort is the same as the algorithm in which lesson?

feedback.correct: Correct. Selection sort uses the comparing-scan logic from 5.4 over and over.
feedback.incorrect: This is the find-the-smallest/largest algorithm you learned in lesson 5.4, applied over and over.

summary: Selection sort finds the smallest in the unsorted part and brings it to the front, again and again.
Only ONE swap is made per pass (its difference from bubble sort).
The "find the smallest" step is the same algorithm as in lesson 5.4.
